deep.reconstruction:
Context: practical astronomy at a transit or meridian instrument in Göttingen. The previous page has thread-transit times of α Ursae Minoris (Polaris) at upper (O-C) and lower (U-C) culmination on 'Venus-day' (Friday) Oct. 11. A Friday 11 October fits 1861. The next page has level-screw readings, the level calibration (1 division = 1 2/3 arcsec) and the clock rate (4.03 s per day fast). This page computes the instrument settings (circle readings) for two stars.

(1) Data. The latitude of Göttingen is φ = 51°31'48''. The declination of Polaris is δ = 88°34'2'', which fits about 1861.

(2) Polaris at lower culmination. Riemann writes 90°+φ = 141°31'48'' (later struck through). He also forms 180°−δ = 91°25'58'' (the 'x' line), i.e. 90° plus the polar distance p = 1°25'58''. The difference is 141°31'48'' − 91°25'58'' = 50°5'50''. This is the true altitude at lower culmination: h_LC = φ − p = φ + δ − 90°. Hence the heading 'Einstellung für den Polarstern 50°5''.

(3) Refraction for Polaris. The mean refraction at h ≈ 50° is 0'.8 (about 58'' cot 50° ≈ 49''). The apparent altitude is therefore 50°5'50'' + 0'.8 ≈ 50°6'.6. Riemann's '6',6' is exactly 5'50'' + 0'.8 = 5'.83 + 0'.8 = 6'.63 (my reading).

(4) Index error. A 'Collimationsfehler' entry is struck out and replaced by 'Indexfehler +1'.4', the zero-point correction of the circle.

(5) Second star. Riemann adds 141°31'48'' + 12°58'44''. He first writes 154°30'0'' and then corrects it to 154°30'32''. He then rounds the corrected value to 154°32' and pairs it with 20h10m13s.
- 20h10m13s is a right ascension (sidereal transit time).
- The quantity 12°58'44'' is a declination magnitude.
- These match α (α²) Capricorni for about 1861: RA ≈ 20h10m, δ ≈ −12°59'. J2000 values (20h18m03s, −12°32'41'') precessed back about 140 years give roughly that.
- So 154°30'32'' = 90° + φ + |δ| is the circle setting for α Cap in the same convention as step (2). The corresponding altitude is 180° − 154°30'32'' = 25°29'28'' = 90° − φ + δ.
- The step from 154°30'32'' to 154°32' (+1.5') is a correction. It is most plausibly the index error +1'.4 (giving 154°31'56''), or possibly refraction (about 2' at 25.5°). The exact convention cannot be settled from the page.

(6) Left column. The entries Δ 121.29, 1h48', 47'.45, 1,6 [over a struck-out figure] and 35 are fragmentary auxiliary numbers whose meaning cannot be fixed. They are perhaps clock or interval differences related to the Polaris thread times on the previous page.

Purpose: preparing the instrument (circle settings for Polaris at lower culmination and for α Cap at upper culmination) for time and azimuth determination at Göttingen. This is routine observatory work.
errors: No real errors. 154°30'0'' was a slip that Riemann himself corrected to 154°30'32'' (48''+44'' = 1'32'').
The final rounding to 154°32' does not equal 154°30'32'' + 1'.4 exactly (that gives 154°31'56''). It is acceptable as a setting to the nearest minute.

results.what: Altitude of Polaris at lower culmination: h = φ + δ − 90° = 50°5'50'' for Göttingen
results.modern_name: meridian altitude of a circumpolar star at lower culmination

results.what: Mean refraction correction of about 0'.8 at 50° altitude, giving apparent altitude 50°6'.6
Circle setting 154°30'32'' (≈154°32' after index correction) for a star at RA 20h10m13s, |δ| = 12°58'44'' (α Capricorni)

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine observatory reductions: latitude plus or minus polar distance, a refraction correction and an index error, done for setting a transit instrument. It is of mild biographical interest that Riemann did practical observing at Göttingen around 1861, but there is no mathematical novelty.

checkable.asserts: supplement of the α Cap setting = 25°29'28'' = 90° − φ − |δ|

transcription_corrections: '141 31 48 / 12 58 44 / 154·30 0' should be read as 154·30 0 with '30 0' overwritten. The intended sum is 154°30'32'', as written on the next line.
'Zi[?] / 0' may be a residual marginal note. It is not part of the computations.
'x 91°25'58''' is 180° − δ(Polaris), not a multiplication. The 'x' is a marker.
'Refraction' above the struck '141°31'48''' line is correct ('Refraction 0',8').
Left-column 'I,6' is probably '1,6' written over another digit.
